summary.motive: Turn an off-coverage corner's cushion into free yardage with a timed slant-flat stretch.
summary.whyItWorks: The flat route forces the corner to choose; whichever way he leans, one receiver occupies him while the other runs into the space he vacated.
summary.failureMode: The corner sits on the slant instead of widening, or press coverage disrupts the timing before the three-step drop can finish.

beats.title: 1. The Rhythm Drop
beats.text: The quarterback takes his three big steps without ever leaving his footwork rhythm. The play is designed to be thrown at the top of the drop no matter what.

beats.title: 2. The Leverage Question
beats.text: The flanker shoots the flat instantly, putting the Cover 2 corner in a bind: widen with the flat or sit on the slant lane. He chooses the flat.

beats.title: 3. The Slant Window Opens
beats.text: As the corner widens, X snaps downfield and drives at the guard's outside hip — exactly where both linebackers are a beat late to close.

beats.title: 4. The Catch on the Move
beats.text: The ball arrives in stride at the top of the drop. X is running north with blockers ahead — the West Coast philosophy made physical: a pass that runs like a run.

relations.tell: The flanker releases flat on his first step and the ball is out within 1.2 seconds — anything slower means the defense triggered correctly.
